takeaway: The common peroneal nerve winds round the fibular neck. Injury causes loss of ankle dorsiflexion and foot eversion: foot drop with a high-stepping gait.

question.text: After a fractured neck of fibula from a side impact, what would you most likely find on examination?
question.say: A man has a fractured neck of fibula after a side impact. What would you most likely find on examination?

lines.text: The side impact crushes the door into the lateral knee and fractures the neck of the fibula.
The common peroneal nerve winds around the neck of the fibula.
So this fracture is the classic way to damage it.
The nerve supplies the lateral and anterior compartments of the leg.
Those muscles dorsiflex the ankle and evert the foot.
With the nerve damaged, he cannot dorsiflex, giving foot drop and a high stepping gait.
